item.title: Reconstruction of pion polarizabilities in lattice QCD with machine learning
item.description: arXiv:2611.13117v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We apply the denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) from generative machine learning to a model-independent reconstruction of electric and magnetic polarizabilities of both charged and neutral pions. The inputs are the sparse momentum-space four-point-function data in lattice QCD for the connected quark-line contributions obtained in previous simulations at four pion masses between approximately 370 and 1100 MeV on quenched Wilson lattices. For charged pions, the elastic contribution is obtained from the pion form-factor slope, and the complete electric and magnetic inelastic terms are reconstructed separately. The neutral-pion electric and magnetic channels are reconstructed without an elastic charge-radius contribution. Four distinct families of synthetic training functions are employed, so that no single analytic fitting function is prescribed for the lattice data. We present low-momentum reconstructions to the limit of zero momentum transfer where the polarizabilities are defined, and mass extrapolations to the physical pion mass of 138 MeV.
item.dc:creator: Hanxing Jiang, Frank X. Lee

item.title: Assessing the expressive power of a gauge-invariant PEPS ansatz across a topological phase transition
item.description: arXiv:2611.13852v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the expressive power of the gauged Gaussian fermionic projected entangled pair state (GGFPEPS) ansatz, which is a manifestly gauge-invariant tensor network ansatz for $(2+1)$-dimensional lattice gauge theories. In the GGFPEPS ansatz, the gauge field on each link is represented by coupling its configuration to the fermion number of virtual fermions placed at both ends of the link. This ansatz has been studied by variational Monte Carlo (VMC) methods in previous work~\cite{Emonts:2022yom}. However, the statistical error of VMC makes a precise determination of the variational parameters difficult, so that the expressive power of the ansatz could not be examined accurately. In this work, we reformulate the computation as a Grassmann tensor network (TN), in which the whole network is contracted deterministically, and introduce the higher-order tensor renormalization group (HOTRG), which allows us to perform calculations in large volumes up to $L=34$. We also evaluate the infinite volume system using the corner transfer matrix renormalization group (CTMRG). We find that the ansatz with only eight complex variational parameters accurately describes the pure $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge theory including the region of the topological phase transition, not only in the energy but also in the topological entanglement entropy. The critical coupling obtained from the peaks of their susceptibilities agrees quantitatively with the one predicted by continuous-time quantum Monte Carlo simulations~\cite{wu2012phase}. Furthermore, near the transition point, we show that the ansatz represents a state outside the plaquette product family, which is a one-parameter family of states assumed in the construction of the ansatz as a simple interpolation between the strong and weak coupling limits.
item.dc:creator: Etsuko Itou, Tsuyoshi Okubo

item.title: Lattice Hamiltonians for Chiral Gauge Theories
item.description: arXiv:2611.13886v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a lattice Hamiltonian for chiral gauge theories on the boundary of a slab. The formulation is gauge-fixed, so the gauge variables are the physical modes of the boundary field, and Gauss's law holds exactly. The bulk gauge field is determined by the boundary field and an integer label, which is the topological charge that the boundary generates and the bulk stores as a localized instanton. The bulk enters as a dielectric, and both gauge anomaly conditions become the question of whether the boundary satisfies Gauss's law on its own. For background gauge fields, we show that sectors that differ by a unit of bulk charge are degenerate after Pauli-Villars subtraction and the mirror fermions decouple. The boundary theory has no vacuum angle. Every term in the Hamiltonian is defined in terms of the boundary gauge variables, the integer label and the fermion modes, a starting point for quantum circuit construction.
item.dc:creator: Dorota M. Grabowska

item.title: Pseudoscalar meson masses in magnetic fields at zero temperature from lattice QCD
item.description: arXiv:2611.14080v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study neutral and charged pseudoscalar meson masses in background magnetic fields in $(2+1)$-flavor QCD at zero temperature and physical quark masses. Using the highly improved staggered quark action at four lattice spacings, we obtain continuum-extrapolated masses from connected correlators for pions, kaons, and the fictitious $s\bar s$ pseudoscalar $\eta^0_{s\bar s}$. Neutral pseudoscalar masses decrease with increasing magnetic field, with the largest relative reduction for the neutral pion. In contrast, charged pion and kaon masses initially rise but tend to level off or decrease at stronger fields, departing from the point-particle lowest-Landau-level expectation. To investigate the origin of this field dependence, we compare neutral and charged pion masses at finite lattice spacings with the field included only in valence propagators or only in the sea-quark determinant. Valence-only masses approximately reproduce the full results, while sea-only masses remain close to their corresponding zero-field values.
item.dc:creator: Heng-Tong Ding, Dan Zhang

item.title: Nucleon sigma terms in lattice QCD at physical pion mass and in the continuum
item.description: arXiv:2611.14103v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the light, strange and charm $\sigma$-terms of the nucleon in lattice QCD using four $N_f=2+1+1$ twisted-mass gauge ensembles simulated at physical pion masses and with approximately the same spatial volumes. The four lattice spacings ranging from $0.080$ fm to $0.049$ fm, with an action that has O(a) improvement, enable extrapolating the results to the continuum limit. Both valence and sea quark contributions are analysed accounting for excited-state contamination from low-lying multihadron states. We perform global fits to all ensembles, that yield $\sigma_{\pi N}=53.0(7.4)(1.6)$ MeV, $\sigma_s=58.2(17.0)(2.1)$ MeV and $\sigma_c=112(28)(25)$ MeV, with statistical and systematic uncertainties, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Constantia Alexandrou, Christos Iona, Giannis Koutsou, Yan Li, Srijit Paul, Ferenc Pittler

item.title: Non-perturbative renormalization of the energy-momentum tensor in the 2d $O(3)$ non-linear $\sigma$-model
item.description: arXiv:2611.14324v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct the traceless components of the energy-momentum tensor on the lattice for the two-dimensional $O(3)$ non-linear $\sigma$-model, such that their correlation functions satisfy the appropriate Ward identities in the continuum limit. The theory is defined by the standard lattice discretizations of both the action and the energy-momentum tensor. The discretization of space-time entails that the traceless two-index symmetric irreducible representation of $O(2)$ splits into two irreducible representations of the dihedral group $D_4$, each requiring an independent renormalization constant. These constants are defined non-perturbatively by imposing discretized versions of continuum Ward identities for one-point functions in the presence of shifted boundary conditions. The non-perturbative calculations are then carried out by Monte Carlo simulations, and the resulting renormalization constants are determined with a final accuracy better than a permille throughout the investigated range of the dimensionless bare coupling constant squared $0\leq g_0^2\leq 0.6$.
item.dc:creator: Leonardo Giusti, Mitsuaki Hirasawa, Michele Pepe

item.title: Variance reduction with probing and Multilevel Monte Carlo in Lattice QCD
item.description: arXiv:2607.05157v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Trace estimation is central in many lattice QCD computations, but the accuracy of the standard, stochastic Hutchinson method improves only with the square root of the sample size, making precise results expensive. We investigate two complementary variance reduction strategies. First, multigrid multilevel Monte Carlo uses a multigrid hierarchy to construct an unbiased multilevel estimator via recursive coarse grid corrections available from the multigrid hierarchy of the solver. Second, stochastic probing uses distance-$d$ graph colorings; we propose a torus based coloring that requires substantially fewer colors than hierarchical probing at the same distance. We test these approaches on two representative problems: the connected pseudoscalar correlator and disconnected fermion loops. For the connected pseudoscalar two-point function, the multilevel decomposition yields a variance reduction of up to $\mathcal{O}(10^5)$ at large time separations and translates into a clear cost reduction at fixed accuracy, thus confirming earlier results of arXiv:2412.06347. For the disconnected loops, in contrast, the multilevel decomposition provides only moderate gains, whereas probing combined with dilution delivers a substantial cost reduction that improves as the number of probing vectors is increased. Overall, the results highlight a pronounced complementarity: deflation schemes are most effective for observables dominated by long distance propagation, while probing is most effective for localized quantities.
item.dc:creator: Andreas Frommer, Jose Jimenez-Merchan, Bruno Lang, Mario Papace, Gustavo Ramirez-Hidalgo

item.title: Negative-Power Density of States in Chiral-Orthogonal Disordered Systems and the IR Phase of QCD
item.description: arXiv:2610.35524v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The recently discovered IR phase of QCD is characterized by an infrared (IR) sector of Dirac modes that separates and dynamically decouples from the bulk of the spectrum, becoming scale invariant in the process [1]. Among key features of this IR sector is the negative power-law behavior of Dirac spectral density near zero with power close to $-1$. Here we start investigating to what extent can this behavior be mimicked by chiral Anderson models. In particular, we study 3-D chiral-orthogonal systems with logarithmic off-diagonal disorder where negative-power ``spikes'' have been observed [2]. We find that for disorders of moderate strength $W$, these models in fact do not have a power-singular density of states (DOS) at zero energy in the thermodynamic limit. Rather, the corresponding power vanishes but the spectrum features a very accurate negative-power behavior on an interval around $E=1$, spreading increasingly closer to $E=0$ and $E=\infty$ with increasing $W$. We connect this to the fact that random hoppings $t$ in these quantum systems are drawn from a scale-invariant $1/t$ distribution regularized via $t \in [e^{-W/2}, e^{W/2}]$, and DOS with negative power can naturally arise inside that range. In fact, we find that power $p$ in the vicinity of energy $E$ satisfies $\lim_{W \to \infty} p(W, E) = -1$ for all $E$ we access. This indicates that, upon removing the cutoff $W$, quantum mechanics transforms the scale-invariant $1/t$ noise into a scale-invariant $1/E$ distribution of eigenstates, which mimics the interpretation of scale-invariant Dirac spectral densities in the IR phase as being due to scale-invariant glue backgrounds [1]. Our results imply that, when modeling the IR phase, the IR cutoff in chiral Anderson systems needs to be tied to their randomness strength $W$ rather than to their lattice size $L$.
item.dc:creator: Ji\v{r}\'i Adam, Jr., Andrei Alexandru, Navdeep Singh Dhindsa, Ivan Horv\'ath, Frank X. Lee, Nilmani Mathur

item.title: Exact chiral symmetry, non-Hermiticity, and the axial anomaly on the lattice: A symmetry-class criterion for disorder-induced undoubling
item.description: arXiv:2611.05395v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A lattice Dirac operator designed to preserve exact chiral symmetry by weighting the derivative with a quenched random field---the \emph{chiral disordered fermions} (\CDF) of [L.\ Jacobs, Phys.\ Rev.\ Lett.\ \textbf{51}, 172 (1983)]---is reexamined with modern tools. We show that the disorder-averaged operator satisfies $\anticomm{\Deff}{\gfive}=0$ exactly, to all orders in disorder strength. Disorder lifts the doubler degeneracy, driving doublers off the real axis into a complex mass while the physical mode remains protected, but does so through non-Hermiticity rather than a Ginsparg--Wilson relation. Consequently the axial index vanishes in every formulation: the Hermitian trace $\Tr(\gfive D)$, the bi-orthogonal index for non-Hermitian operators, and the algebraic Riesz-projector index, including at exceptional points. The \CDF operator therefore cannot reproduce the axial anomaly: its failure is enforced by the exact chiral symmetry it preserves. We classify neighboring constructions by the Dirac channel carrying the lattice structure. Disorder in the $\g_\mu$ channel preserves chirality, realizes an Altland--Zirnbauer chiral class, and cannot carry an index; disorder in the $\mathbb{1}$ mass channel breaks chiral symmetry and yields Callan--Harvey/domain-wall physics. A one-parameter family interpolates between them, with the 1983 operator and Kaplan's domain wall as opposite limits, distinguished not by disorder itself but by the channel it occupies. This unifies lattice-QCD undoubling with the tenfold-way classification of disordered Dirac fermions and settles the disorder route to chiral lattice fermions.
item.dc:creator: Laurence A. Jacobs

item.title: Finite-volume Analysis of On-shell Subtraction in the Luescher formalism
item.description: arXiv:2611.05899v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: On-shell subtraction is a relevant step in finite-volume analyses, which is to isolate an on-shell singularity and evaluate regular momentum-dependent factors at their on-shell values. For short-range interactions with a finite mass gap, the correction associated with this on-shell subtraction is exponentially suppressed at sufficiently large volume and can therefore be neglected at the corresponding accuracy. We examine how this correction changes as the relevant mass parameter decreases. Using a common dimensional-regularization prescription, we derive analytic expressions for the resulting finite volume correction for representative momentum structures and examine their behavior numerically. For a nonzero mass parameter, the corrections are indeed exponentially suppressed at large $\mu L$, whereas in the massless limit this suppression is replaced by an enhanced finite-volume dependence. More importantly, the $S$-wave contribution can develop an infrared divergence of finite volume correction in the massless limit. These results clarify the conditions under which on-shell subtraction can be applied and provide guidance for assessing such corrections in finite-volume hadronic calculations involving long-range effects, including QCD+QED.
item.dc:creator: Wanchen Lei, Yuting Wang, Jin-Yi Pang

item.title: Diffusion models for the $O(3)$ nonlinear sigma model
item.description: arXiv:2610.39568v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A score-based diffusion model is trained on the two-dimensional classical Heisenberg model, the lattice representation of the $O(3)$ nonlinear sigma model. Neural networks are trained on three different coarse-grainings of the same training set to implement a multiscale sampling scheme that modestly improves both the accuracy and computational cost of direct sampling on the finest lattice. Stein (or Schwinger-Dyson) diagnostics for the two-point correlation function are introduced to assess the quality of the learned score without relying on reverse diffusion sampling. These diagnostics are also incorporated into an additional training loss. We discuss several technical considerations relevant to implementing diffusion models on $S^2$. These include a consideration of lifting the network input to $S^3$, as in the $CP^1$ representation, and developing a boundary-layer approximation to the short-time spherical heat kernel that extends its usefulness to larger diffusion times.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Schubring
